newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends steady, long-dated bonds in demand.
newsitem.headline: India call ends steady, long-dated bonds in demand.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 6.00-7.00 percent on Monday, unchanged from Saturday's closing and down from the day's opening of 7.25-7.75 percent, dealers said.
"Most of the deals were at 7.50 percent and some stray deals at 8.0 percent and some at 6.25 percent," a dealer at a leading lending institution said.
The 13.82 percent 2002 stock and zero coupon bond maturing in 2000 were in limelight, Vinod Dixit at Centurion Bank said.
"Security prices are on the rise and the rally will continue till the Reserve Bank announces a new loan," Dixit said.

The market focus was shifting to the long-dated securities from short-dated ones, Kavita Rahalkar at Birla Marlin Securities said. "Today's volume was 3.65 billion rupees against Saturday's 1.49 billion rupees," she said.
Yield on securities were steady for shorter dated securities but yields fell on longer dated securities, dealers said.
They said the 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded steady at 11.90 percent, but the yield on 13.50 percent 1998 stock fell to 12.63 percent from 12.76 percent.
Treasury bills maturing in October 1997 were traded at 11.60 percent against Saturday's yield of 11.75 percent, dealers said.
There was no activity in commercial paper and certificate of deposits on Monday, dealers said.
Inter-corporate deposits were quoted at 17-18.5 percent for 90 days for P1+ companies, while the P1 companies were quoted in the region of 21-27 percent, dealers said.
